sections.html:
The 2020 census put West Haven's population at 55,584. The shoreline city in New Haven County has 22,735 housing units, and 5.8% of them stood vacant. Median household income was $73,566.

Which part of town a house is in changes who shows up to buy it. Center, around the green and Campbell Avenue, is the main commercial street, and West Shore follows the water. Allingtown is the hilly district around the University of New Haven. Sandy Point is a beach and bird sanctuary reaching into New Haven Harbor. A waterfront house and a hillside house near campus appeal to different people.

Population climbed from 25,808 in 1930 to 52,851 in 1970, so much of the housing dates from those decades. Buyers' inspectors look first at roofs, wiring and heating in houses that old, and you will want to know their condition before the first showing.

sections.h2: Who values your property and who sends the bill
sections.html:
Two offices share the work. The Assessor's Office decides what the property is worth. The Tax Collector mails the bill and takes the money. You will find the Assessor in City Hall at 355 Main Street, 1st floor, at 203-937-3515, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Value, exemption and appeal questions belong to the Assessor, while "what do I owe today" belongs to the Tax Collector. Jot down which one you need before dialing, since a call to the wrong desk is the usual reason people get nowhere.

The Assessor's site also posts a mill rates sheet and a street list sorted by fire district. Open both before you quote anyone a tax figure. Start at the Assessor's Office page.

Assessment topicWest Haven detail
Assessment level70% of fair market value
Most recent revaluationRevaluation 2024
Appeal bodyBoard of Assessment Appeals
Forms offeredAppeals application and representative form
Relief programsState elderly and totally disabled programs, military service exemptions, blind exemption, renters rebate
RecordsOnline assessment records and West Haven GIS

The assessed value on your bill is 70% of market value, so it will look lower than what you expect to sell for. That is normal and does not mean the house is underpriced.

If you think the value is wrong, you file with the Board of Assessment Appeals. The Assessor's page has an application, plus a separate form when someone represents you. Call the Assessor's Office for the current filing window before you plan around it.

After a 2024 revaluation, a sharp rise in the bill is the usual trigger. The Assessor links a Revaluation Questions and Answers page for that, along with the vendor's taxpayer information site. Pull the property record card first. A wrong square footage, bedroom count or lot size can often be fixed by phone, without a formal appeal.

Gather dated photos, plus a recent appraisal or comparable sales if you have them. An argument about condition lands better with pictures than with a description.

sections.h2: Does your fire district change the bill?
sections.html:
Possibly. West Haven bills differ by street because of fire districts. Allingtown's district was absorbed by the city, and two independent ones remain, First Fire Taxation (Center) and West Shore. Each of those levies its own rate.

Find your street on the Assessor's list of streets by fire district, then read the mill rates sheet. For a payoff estimate, tell the Tax Collector the exact address and ask which district and rates apply, and whether a district amount comes on its own bill or with the city's.

Residents have discussed consolidating the districts. Before you promise a buyer a yearly cost, ask whether any change is coming.

For exact due dates, late-payment interest and the balance on your parcel, you need the Tax Collector. Phone before you commit to a sale agreement and get these in writing:

  • the real estate tax balance on the parcel, fire district amount included;
  • the date of each installment and what has been paid;
  • any sewer or other charge recorded against the property;
  • the last day the payoff figure holds, so your closing date does not leave a few days of interest hanging.

File the written payoff with your sale papers. The closing attorney will request the same numbers, and having them early shortens the final week.

On a West Haven sale, the seller files Form OP-236 with the state once the deed is recorded. Tax is owed on prices of $2,000 or more unless an exemption fits. The town code to write on the form is 156.

  • The return can be signed by the grantor, the grantor's attorney or an authorized agent.
  • In participating towns, filing runs through the state's myCTREC portal, and the money is drawn only after recording.
  • Where electronic filing is not offered, both pages of the form go in with a check payable to the Commissioner of Revenue Services.

Two exemptions are worth asking about: a principal residence sold for too little to cover the mortgages, the real estate tax and other liens ahead of them, and a principal residence deeded in lieu of foreclosure. Let your closing attorney choose the code. The DRS conveyance tax page lists them all.

An open tax balance will not block a sale, though it has to be cleared at the table. A sensible sequence:

  1. Request a written payoff from the Tax Collector covering every open balance on the parcel.
  2. Pass that figure to your closing attorney or title company before you sign a contract.
  3. Make sure the payoff appears on the settlement statement and is deducted from your proceeds.
  4. Keep the paid receipt after closing in case anyone asks later.

Cash buyers handle this the same way, since they check title and tax status regardless. Trouble comes from surprises, like a district charge nobody asked about, and an early call prevents most of them.

sections.h2: Papers to gather before you list
sections.html:
A single folder with the right papers saves time with every buyer, agent and attorney you talk to.

  • Your deed and the latest tax bill.
  • The property record card from the Assessor's online records.
  • Receipts or approximate dates for roof, wiring and heating work.
  • Letters confirming any exemption or relief program you receive now.
  • The written tax payoff, once you have it.

If you get an elderly, disabled or military service exemption, tell the buyer it is yours and does not transfer on its own. They will have to apply for their own. Mentioning it up front also keeps them from reading your lower bill as the number they will pay.

faqs.q: Who do I call about West Haven property assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at 203-937-3515. It is on the first floor of City Hall at 355 Main Street and is open Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What percent of value does West Haven assess?
faqs.a: Property is assessed at 70% of fair market value. The most recent revaluation is Revaluation 2024.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal a West Haven assessment?
faqs.a: Appeals go to the Board of Assessment Appeals. The Assessor's page offers an application and a representative form, and the office can tell you the current filing window.

faqs.q: Does a fire district add to a West Haven tax bill?
faqs.a: It can. The two remaining independent fire districts each levy their own rate, and the Assessor posts a street list by fire district. Ask the Tax Collector which one applies to your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Haven house that owes property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a written payoff from the Tax Collector, and the title company can pay the tax from the sale proceeds at closing.
